newsitem.title: USA: Duff may cut Prudential payment ability rating.
newsitem.headline: Duff may cut Prudential payment ability rating.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Friday it may cut its double-A rating on Prudential Insurance Co of America's claims-paying ability.

Duff said it put Prudential on "rating watch -- down" due to continuing uncertainty about the ultimate cost of claims for improper insurance sales practices and the adverse impact on the competitive position of several of Prudential's business units.
Duff said Prudential's healthcare group, property/casualty group and individual life insurance group had been hurt to varying degrees by increasingly competitive markets over the past several years.
"Because of these factors, (Duff's) expectations of the sustainable earnings growth of the company have become less certain," Duff wrote in a report.
Duff said Prudential continues to have a strong capability to raise capital and more than adequate liquidity.

Duff said it continues to monitor closely the progress of the Prudential settlement process, legal proceedings and sales compliance issues. It is also watching the development of strategic initiatives of the company's various business units.
Prudential has entered into a settlement calling for it to pay at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million policyholders who say they were victims of deceptive sales practices.
Four states -- Florida, Massachusetts, Texas and California -- have filed objections to the settlement.
